content.value_statement: Teams need reliable links between requirements, files, and source repositories. This skill extracts spec IDs, titles, hashes, and paths for agent workflows.
actual_capabilities: Scans a primary repository root and optional extra roots for specification files.
Reads specs/ and specs/external-requests/ while skipping specs/templates/.
Extracts requirement IDs and titles from Markdown heading patterns.
Creates traceability metadata with source repo, relative path, anchor link, and file hash.
Sorts manifest entries by repository, path, and requirement ID.
Supports JSON or TOON output according to the skill variables.
limitations: It depends on requirement IDs appearing in supported Markdown heading formats.
It does not define a parser implementation or execute discovery by itself.
It may miss requirements stored outside the configured spec directories.
It reports empty results when specs/ is missing instead of searching the whole repository.

use_cases.title: Create a requirements index
use_cases.description: Build a traceable list of requirement IDs before release planning or scope review.

use_cases.title: Map tests to source requirements
use_cases.description: Find requirement IDs, titles, and file links that support test planning and coverage review.

use_cases.title: Feed traceability data to agents
use_cases.description: Produce a compact manifest that downstream agents can use for implementation and review tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Find specs in this repo
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spec-discovery on the current repository. Return a sorted manifest. Include specs and external requests. Flag duplicate IDs in notes.

prompt_templates.title: Scan multiple repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use spec-discovery with the current repo and an extra shared specs repo. Keep paths relative to each source root. Return TOON output.

prompt_templates.title: Check missing IDs
prompt_templates.prompt: Run spec discovery, then list spec files that produced no IDs. Explain whether each file likely needs heading format fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare agent traceability
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a JSON manifest for all configured repos. Include hashes, anchors, duplicate notes, and source repositories. Optimize the result for agent handoff.

output_examples.input: Scan the current repository for requirements.
output_examples.output: The result is a sorted manifest with each requirement ID, title, source repository, relative path, anchor link, and file hash.

output_examples.input: Find duplicate requirement IDs across two repositories.
output_examples.output: The report lists duplicate IDs in notes and keeps entries grouped by repository and path.

output_examples.input: Create compact output for another agent.
output_examples.output: The answer uses TOON format and preserves ID casing while making anchors lowercase and hyphenated.

best_practices: Set ROOT and EXTRA_REPOS explicitly before running discovery.
Review notes for duplicate IDs before downstream planning.
Prefer JSON when another tool will parse the manifest.
anti_patterns: Do not assume files without supported headings contain no requirements.
Do not scan unrelated repositories without user approval.
Do not edit ID casing when generating anchors or trace links.

faq.question: What files does it scan?
faq.answer: It scans specs/ and specs/external-requests/ under each configured repository. It skips specs/templates/.

faq.question: Which requirement IDs are supported?
faq.answer: It targets Markdown headings that begin with REQ- followed by letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.

faq.question: Does it change files?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes discovery and manifest generation. It does not require modifying source files.

faq.question: Can it work across repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure EXTRA_REPOS to include additional repository roots that contain specification directories.

faq.question: What output formats are available?
faq.answer: It supports JSON for tools and TOON for compact prompt context.

faq.question: What happens when no specs directory exists?
faq.answer: It returns an empty result instead of failing.
